researched.name: Bharat Seats Ltd
researched.reason: ICRA upgraded the long-term rating two notches in fifteen months - [ICRA]A- (Apr-2024) to [ICRA]A (Jun-2025) to [ICRA]A+ Stable (24-Sep-2026) - and raised the rated amount from Rs 134.32 cr to Rs 188.96 cr. The rationale is a growth document, not just a credit one: FY2026 operating income Rs 1,951.0 cr against FY2025's Rs 1,288.8 cr (+51%), PAT Rs 42.2 cr, and an explicit expectation that 'revenue growth is estimated to remain strong at 30-35% in FY2027'. Two independent checks were run on it. First, the sum of the four standalone quarters to March 2026 in this repo's docs/quarterly_results.json - built from the company's own BSE results filings - is Rs 1,950.9 cr of revenue and Rs 42.2 cr of PAT, matching ICRA's audited table. Second, Q1 FY27 as filed on 2026-08-04 is revenue Rs 577.83 cr against Rs 427.06 cr a year earlier, +35.3%, with PAT Rs 13.21 cr against Rs 9.18 cr, +43.9% - at the TOP of ICRA's range, so the growth is measured rather than forecast. The identified driver is specific: 2W wheel assembly went from Rs 55 cr (FY2025) to Rs 321 cr (FY2026) and BSL became SMIPL's ONLY wheel-assembly vendor from April 2026, on top of five new MSIL models won with FY2027-FY2029 start of production. On the model, FY2027 revenue of Rs 2,536-2,634 cr at a 2.0-2.2% PAT margin (the last two audited years were 2.5% and 2.2%, and ICRA says margins stay range-bound) gives EPS Rs 8.08-9.23 and a forward PE of 23.2-26.5x on 6.2802 cr shares at Rs 213.95 - against a peer cohort of similarly thin-margin OEM suppliers computed this run at 26-46x trailing (Wheels India 36.7x on a 2.8% margin, TVS Srichakra 38.1x on 2.6%, JTEKT 46.1x on 2.6%, Lumax 31.6x on 3.9%, and NDR Auto - BSL's own 28.6% shareholder - 32.0x). The stock closed DOWN 1.9% on the day of the upgrade, 15.9% below its 65-day high, on 0.3x normal volume, with FII 0.15% and DII 0.22%: nothing has been discounted. Held at medium rather than high because about 90% of revenue rests on two Suzuki-group customers on a 2.2% net margin, margins are falling as the mix shifts to wheel assembly, Rs 65 cr of the FY27 capex debt is still unsanctioned by ICRA's own footnote, and no annual report, concall or investor deck could be read today - api.bseindia.com was 403 from both the sandbox and Actions, so pledge, auditor remarks, promoter remuneration and related-party pricing are all unknown.

researched.name: Harrisons Malayalam Ltd
researched.reason: NOT PUBLISHED - the exposure is documented and large, and the pass-through is measurably absent. The FY2025-26 annual report (193 pages, filed with NSE 2026-09-04) was read: note 41 gives rubber external revenue of Rs 292.68 cr against tea Rs 242.32 cr and others Rs 4.08 cr, so rubber is 54.3% of Rs 539.08 cr of external revenue, and rubber segment profit of Rs 25.64 cr against a tea segment LOSS of Rs 0.69 cr means rubber carries essentially all the profit. The Directors' Report gives the physical numbers: own-garden rubber crop 4,341 MT in FY2026 against 4,800 MT in FY2025, bought rubber 4,020 MT against 3,062 MT, and 'the average price realized per kg of rubber was Rs 214.84 as against Rs 216.19 realized during the previous year'. So this is a genuine producer of the commodity that moved, at the right market cap. It fails on transmission, on three measured counts. (1) THE QUARTER ALREADY REPORTED CONTRADICTS THE THESIS. Kottayam RSS4 averaged Rs 253.72/kg in Q1 FY27 against Rs 197.30/kg for the whole of FY2026 - 28.6% higher - and in that quarter Harrisons' revenue rose only 7.3% (Rs 116.46 cr to Rs 124.92 cr) while operating profit FELL 30.7% (Rs 8.21 cr to Rs 5.69 cr) and PAT fell 33.9% (Rs 5.96 cr to Rs 3.94 cr). Kerala rubber tapping is seasonal and Q1 is the low-crop quarter, which may explain part of it, but the quarterly filings carry no crop split so that defence cannot be tested - it stays a hypothesis, and the only measurement available points the wrong way. (2) FY2026 ITSELF SHOWED THE SAME. Rubber segment profit fell from Rs 35.44 cr to Rs 25.64 cr on an almost flat realisation, as cost of material consumed in the segment rose from Rs 60.21 cr to Rs 76.97 cr; and about 48% of rubber tonnage handled is BOUGHT (4,020 of 8,361 MT), which buys at the same rising market it sells into. Plantation costs are not fixed here. (3) THE PRICE HAS STALLED. Rs 277.00/kg today is +40.4% on the FY26 average for the current quarter but only +1.1% over a month and +1.8% over three, and it sits 2.5% below the 2026-08-01 series high of Rs 284.00. Two further practical objections: turnover in the stock on 2026-09-25 was Rs 8.08 lakh, well under the PLAYBOOK's Rs 25 lakh floor; and the annual report carries heavy land litigation - a Government of Kerala civil suit over 5,882 hectares of Wayanad tea estates, a 707-hectare surplus-land order remanded by the High Court, 1,074 hectares under lease challenge, 415 hectares held surplus in Tamil Nadu, and 140 hectares of planted rubber at Kumbazha encroached since 2007 and still untapped. One arithmetic gap is recorded rather than bridged: rubber goods revenue of Rs 275.95 cr over 8,361 MT implies about Rs 330/kg, which does not reconcile with the disclosed realisation of Rs 214.84/kg, and the annual report does not define its MT figures well enough to close it. That is an unknown, not a number to invent. Verdict: documented exposure, unverified transmission - the right place for this is the watch list until a quarter shows the realisation actually rising.
